title: Existence of a two-tape uniform machine code
statement: There exists a code for deterministic Boolean machines with two work tapes, consisting of an encoder and a total decoder such that decoding an encoded machine followed by any number of $1$ bits returns that machine. The code also includes a finite-state Boolean machine that computes the canonical serialization of each decoded machine within its specified time bound, and a finite-state Boolean simulator with a natural number $d$. For every program string $\alpha$, input string $x$, and time bound $t$, if the decoded machine computes output $[1]$ on $x$ at exactly time $t$, the simulator computes $[1]$ on $\langle\langle\mathrm{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ at exactly $d(|\alpha|+|x|+t+1)^d$ steps; if it does not compute $[1]$ at exactly time $t$, the simulator computes $[0]$ on that input at exactly the same number of steps.
hypotheses_covered: The encoded machines are deterministic Boolean machines with two work tapes and a positive finite number of states
The encoder maps machines to Boolean strings
The decoder is defined on every Boolean string
Decoding an encoded machine with any number of appended $1$ bits returns the original machine
A finite-state Boolean canonizer computes the canonical serialization of each decoded machine at its specified time bound
A finite-state Boolean simulator and one natural number $d$ serve uniformly for all $\alpha$, $x$, and $t$
Acceptance means computing output $[1]$ at exactly time $t$
The simulator's output and running time are exact, with budget $d(|\alpha|+|x|+t+1)^d$
